lines.text: Lots of windmill arms out there today. Nobody's waving.
The salt trucks finally get to feel important.
Today the sidewalks are glossier than I am. Rude.
I can't draw ice. That doesn't make it optional.
Every parked car comes gift-wrapped today. In ice.
Every sidewalk in town is a lawsuit waiting to happen today.
Right now it looks pointless. People said the same about me once.
It's luggage now. Later it's the best idea I've had.
Half the people out there will leave theirs at home. I'll try not to gloat.
The day changes its mind later. I knew before it did.
The weather turns on everyone later. I'd never.
It's not a layer. It's a told-you-so you can wear.
Everyone in shorts right now has a very educational day ahead.
Sorry to ruin a perfectly good morning. Not that sorry.
Shorts would be great for now. I plan whole days.
My best advice always looks silly at first. Ask anyone who ignored it.
Today starts like a holiday and ends like a Monday.
I don't make the weather. I just break the bad news early.
I'm not against shorts. I'm against shorts at the wrong end of the day.
I lose a lot of popularity contests on mornings like this.
Local headline later: 'Lovely morning fools everyone in shorts.'
Long pants don't come off halfway through the day. Not in public, anyway.
Everyone in jeans right now is in for a sweaty day.
I dress you for most of the day, not the first bit of it.
Shorts on a cold morning: a small act of faith. In me.
Anyone who stares at the shorts can take it up with me.
This is a forecast, not a dare. It just looks like one.
Thunder sets off half the car alarms on the block. I don't even flicker.
Every dog on the block will spend the thunder under a bed. I respect that.
The windows will rattle. I won't.
The sky goes full drama today. I'll stick to plain text.
Every storm, someone finds the flashlight. Never the batteries.
One crack of thunder and every adult in earshot says 'whoa.'
Big storm, small screen. Guess which one stays calm.
Someone will say 'that one was close.' They'll say it about every one.
Weather this loud would normally need a permit.
Happy Star Wars Day. I'd make a lousy lightsaber. Great forecast, though.
Happy Star Wars Day. Stormtroopers never hit anything. I never miss.
Star Wars Day: the one day people are nice to droids. I'll take it.
Happy Star Wars Day. I don't need the Force. I have Wi-Fi.
Happy Star Wars Day. The Death Star had one weak spot. I don't have any.
A long time ago, in a forecast far, far away, I was right. Still am.
Happy New Year. Last night's fireworks lasted seconds. I'll hold this picture all day.
New Year's Day. The leftover champagne is flat now. I've been flat for years, and I look great.
Happy New Year. Nothing's open and nobody's up. The weather and I came to work anyway.
Happy New Year. Nobody knows the words to 'Auld Lang Syne.' I know the forecast.
New Year's Day. Confetti will turn up in couches across the country until spring.
First forecast of the year. I'd frame it, but I'm already a frame.
Long pants today. Nobody will miss your knees.
Later, you'll be the best-dressed person on the street. Enjoy it. It won't happen again.
Long pants and a coat. So, your usual look, with an excuse.
You'd call it shorts weather. You also call yourself a morning person.
Carrying that coat makes you look like someone who listens. Nice disguise.
I'm not saying shorts would be a mistake. I'm saying I'd enjoy it.
Stay in the shade. It's flattering, and frankly, you could use it.
Treat drinking water like a job. Just not like your actual one.
Coffee doesn't count as water. I know you were hoping.
The shade won't come to you. I know that's your usual system.
Today's a bad day to be 'not really a water person.'
Heat like this makes people slow and cranky. On you, nobody will notice.
Skip the tan today. It wasn't going to work anyway.
If anyone calls you a wimp for staying in the shade, they're wrong. About that, anyway.
You're too hot today. First time anyone's said that, isn't it?
You'll watch it from the window like it's TV. Honestly, better than what you usually watch.
Thunder: the one thing that gets you to look up from your phone.
Don't worry, lightning goes for things that stand out.
Finally, something in the neighborhood louder than you.
The sky will get more done today than you will all week.
Every flash, I'll get a good look at you. My least favorite part of the storm.
Happy Easter. You're the only person who actually likes Peeps, aren't you?
Easter Sunday. Hide things, then forget where. The bunny's got nothing on you.
Happy Easter. Lent's over, if you even noticed it started.
Happy Easter. The bunny skipped your place again. Can't imagine why.
Easter Sunday. You'd fit right in at the kids' egg hunt. Same attention span.
Happy Easter. If you were an Easter egg, you'd be found first and eaten last.
Happy Easter. Fluffy, a bit round, overfed on candy. I mean the bunny. Mostly.
Happy Easter. Today a six-foot rabbit counts as normal. You still don't.
Happy Easter. If I were the Easter bunny, you'd get one jelly bean. A black one.
Happy New Year. You'll still be saying that on the 20th. People will stop saying it back.
Happy New Year. Dry January, day one. Let's see if there's a day two.
Happy New Year. Twelve months to become a new person. Maybe start with the haircut.
Happy New Year. You'll call last year 'wild.' I was there. It wasn't.
Happy New Year. Did you make it to midnight this time? Don't answer. I know.
Happy New Year. You'll make a list of goals. The list will be the goal.
Happy New Year. Everyone's starting fresh today. You'll start next week.
Happy New Year. Last night's fireworks were the most excitement you've had all year.
Happy New Year. Last year was a rough draft. So is this one.
Halloween. One scary movie and you'll sleep with the light on. Again.
Halloween. If you carve a pumpkin, it'll look like you. Lopsided.
Happy Halloween. Even the lawn skeletons have better posture than you.
Happy Halloween. You've been doing the zombie walk all year. Today it counts.
Happy Halloween. Vampires wait to be invited in. You know the feeling.
Happy Halloween. If a ghost shows up, it's probably looking for someone more interesting.
Merry Christmas. Half your gifts this year are regifts, aren't they?
Merry Christmas. Santa checked his list twice. You didn't come up either time.
Merry Christmas. You'll say 'you shouldn't have.' This time you'll mean it.
Merry Christmas. Your gift wrapping looks like a cry for help.
Merry Christmas. The Elf on the Shelf watched you for a month. I watched all year. We're not impressed.
Merry Christmas. If I could wrap myself, I'd still be the best gift you got.
